external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
external_entities.notes: Shoppers sign in with email and password and receive a session cookie. MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment-status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that shoppers use to browse and place orders and that receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: It is the only thing exposed to the internet. It handles shopper email/password sign-in and session cookies.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive
data_stores.notes: Each receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A shopper signs in to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: A shopper browses through the storefront API.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper places an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service for a shopper-submitted order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read-write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders and related shopper and payment data in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a completed-order receipt to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a payment-settlement webhook to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party environment controlling the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database's stated contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It stores shopper addresses, card-last-four values, and orders.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive's stated contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It stores receipts associated with completed orders.

assumptions.assumption: The card processor is in a separate tenant-controlled trust zone.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly describes the card processor as a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The card processor trust zone is tenant-separated because it is controlled by a different party.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the card processor as a third party.
